title: Cloudflare, GitHub, and Nathan AI Rocket 🚀
outcome: Draw a fleet diagram that distinguishes physical mining, monitoring and code delivery.
show: Place authorized ASICs and the pool on one row. Put Cloudflare telemetry and GitHub source and tests on a second row.
concepts: A fleet record names an owned or expressly authorized device, its model and assigned operator. A Super 2X or Hyper slot counts capacity in the plan. Operational counts require actual inventory and observations.
Workers can serve the dashboard, verify a public header and report health. A dispatch namespace gives a development Worker a separate deployment target.
GitHub holds code and runs project tests. GitHub Actions terms prohibit cryptomining, including on self-hosted Actions runners.
replicate: Trace the legitimate records for one device from inventory to a pool-acknowledged share.
On the diagram, mark where to display an offline device, an unassigned slot and an accepted share. Give each a distinct status.
check: What evidence upgrades a planned slot to a mining endpoint?
An authorized real device with a confirmed inventory identity and evidence that its configured pool is receiving work.
sources: Cloudflare Workers for Platforms · Dynamic dispatch

challenge.title: Route the fleet work
challenge.prompt: Send each task to the part of Nathan AI Rocket 🚀 that can carry it out.
cards: Search for a fresh Bitcoin proof and submit shares
Mining hardware and the pool exchange jobs and shares.
Show observed device status and public proof checks
An application can publish telemetry and verify existing public headers.
Keep source code and run a fixed proof-validation test
The repository and its tests support development.
Acknowledge a share sent by an enrolled miner
The configured pool acknowledges its submitted shares.
challenge.tip: Track hardware, live dashboard evidence, and software development as distinct parts of the fleet.
